# CopyPrompt

A ready-made prompt in the page's own type, with a button that copies it, for the person to hand to an agent of their own. The prompt wraps as prose, keeping its line breaks, and the button is `CopyButton`: it copies through the Clipboard API or a text selection, says "Copied" for two seconds, and screen readers hear it once. Screen readers hear the prompt as the button's description, so several prompts on a page stay apart.

```tsx
import { CopyPrompt } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/copy-prompt/copy-prompt";
```

## Example

```tsx
<CopyPrompt text="Suggest a layout for my mornings: customer chats first, then my calendar." />
```

## Use instead when

- Use `CodeBlock` instead for code or a command, in the monospace font, and `CopyButton` alone to copy a value shown elsewhere.

## Props

Type: `CopyPromptProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: margins, width, grid placement (`mt-2`). Appearance classes warn in development. |
| `copiedLabel` | `string` | `"Copied"` | What the button says, and screen readers hear, once the prompt is on the clipboard. |
| `failedLabel` | `string` | `"Couldn't copy"` | What the button says, and screen readers hear, when the browser refused to copy. |
| `label` | `string` | `"Copy"` | The copy button's label. Screen readers hear the prompt as its description. |
| `onCopy` | `((text: string) => void)` |  | Called with the prompt once it is on the clipboard. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` |  | Reaches the rendered element. |
| `text` (required) | `string` |  | The prompt, as plain text: what the person pastes into their agent. Line breaks show as written. |

## Native attributes

Also accepts the attributes in React's `HTMLAttributes` (`id`, `aria-*`, event handlers), passed to the rendered element, except those named on this page.

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `prompt`: Not a prop. The prompt is `text`: `<CopyPrompt text="Suggest a layout for my mornings.">`.
- `value`: Not a prop. The prompt is `text`: `<CopyPrompt text="Suggest a layout for my mornings.">`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`). Your classes always win over Ouro UI's: CopyPrompt merges `className` last with `cn` (tailwind-merge), so a class that conflicts with its own replaces it.[^layout-classes]

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.
